en: The Apadāna of the Elder Sabbadāyaka Pilindavaccha Chapter 9, Number 9 [Verse 1] I was a king named Mahāpabbata, A ruler of the earth, endowed with great power. I gave away all my wealth, And then I went forth into homelessness. [Verse 2] Having gone forth, I practiced the holy life Under the Teacher, the Great Sage. For eighty-four thousand years I maintained the practice of celibacy. [Verse 3] When I had completed that holy life, I passed away from that human existence. I was reborn in the Brahma world, Possessing a lifespan of eighty-four thousand aeons. [Verse 4] From that Brahma world, having passed away, I was reborn among humans. There too, for eighty-four thousand years, I maintained the practice of celibacy. [Verse 5] In this way, throughout many hundreds of thousands of births, I never experienced a state of woe. Having performed deeds of merit, I have now attained the fruit of Arhatship. [Verse 6] I am the Elder Sabbadāyaka; My name is well-known in the world. Through the power of that gift, I have attained the fruit of Arhatship. [Verse 7] I am the Elder Sabbadāyaka; My name is well-known in the world. “Having plunged into the great ocean,
my abode was well-constructed;
the lotus pond was well-constructed.”
Resounding with the cries of ruddy geese,
it was covered with mandārava flowers and with pink and blue lotuses.
And there a river flows, with beautiful, well-situated banks,
covered over with fish and turtles.
It was filled with the gathering of various birds,
resounding with the cries of peacocks and cranes,
and the sweet songs of cuckoos and other warblers.
Pigeons, sun-birds, ruddy geese, river-dwelling cranes,
mynas, and mainas are there as well.
Pampakas and jīvajīvakas;
swans and cranes were crying out,
along with many kosiya and piṅgala birds.
Endowed with the seven treasures,
with sands of gems and pearls,
and with trees made entirely of gold.
Stirred by various fragrances,
they illuminate the palace day and night at all times.
Sixty thousand musical instruments resounded morning and evening;
sixteen thousand women—
They always attend upon me.
Having gone forth from my abode,
[I saw] Sumedha, the Leader of the World.
With a clear mind and joyful heart,
I paid homage to that one of great renown;
having saluted the Perfectly Enlightened One, I—
I invited him along with the Saṅgha;
that wise one, Sumedha, the leader of the world, accepted.
Having delivered a discourse on the Dhamma,
the Great Sage dismissed him;
having paid homage to the Fully Enlightened One, [he departed].
I approached my dwelling and addressed my attendants:
"All of you, assemble together."
In the morning, the Buddha will come to our abode.
It is a gain for us; it is well-acquired by us.
We who dwell in your presence;
may we too perform worship for the Teacher, the Supreme Buddha.”
Having prepared food and drink,
I announced the time to him along with one hundred thousand masters.
The Leader of the World approached.
I went out to meet him with the fivefold musical instruments.
The Supreme Person sat upon a seat made entirely of gold;
there was a canopy above.
Then, made entirely of gold,
fans were fanned within the community of monks.
I satisfied the community of monks with abundant food and drink,
and [offered] pairs of individual garments.
I gave it to the community of monks.
To him whom they call Sumedha,
the recipient of the world’s offerings;
Having sat down in the community of bhikkhus,
he spoke these verses:
“He who [serves] me with food and drink...”
I have satisfied all these beings;
I shall proclaim that,
so listen to me as I speak.
For eighteen hundred eons,
he will delight in the world of the gods;
and a thousand times he will be a king.
He will become a wheel-turning monarch.
Whichever womb he enters—
whether that of a deity or a human—
He will always wear a covering made entirely of gold for thirty thousand eons.
Born of the Okkāka clan,
he will be a teacher in the world named Gotama by lineage.
He is the heir to the Dhamma,
the legitimate son, fashioned by the Dhamma;
having fully understood all taints, he has abandoned them.
Free from taints, he will attain Nibbāna;
seated within the Saṅgha of bhikkhus,
he will roar the lion’s roar.
They hold a parasol over you;
stay beneath the parasol!
I have attained the state of a recluse.
The defilements have been burnt away by me;
whether in a pavilion or at the foot of a tree,
no feverish distress exists for me.
During thirty thousand aeons,
whatever gift I gave at that time,
I have not known a miserable rebirth.
This is the fruit of all my giving.
My defilements have been incinerated... [and so forth].
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me... [and so forth].
This is the teaching of the Buddha:
the four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Sabbadāyaka recited these verses.
The legend of the elder Sabbadāyaka is the ninth.
